```{r setup, include=FALSE}
root<-normalizePath(getwd())
while(!file.exists(file.path(root,'R/heldout_influence.R'))) {p<-dirname(root);if(p==root)stop('Repository not found');root<-p}
.libPaths(c(file.path(root,'_output/R-library'),.libPaths()))
library(data.table)
source(file.path(root,'R/heldout_influence_presentation.R'))
x<-load_heldout_influence(root)
```

**Descriptive and post hoc.** This appendix uses the existing available-window county totals and the original missing-kept masks for unscreened, |z| > 2, mid-p < 0.10 and pre-RMSE top 10%. No model is refitted, target reconstructed, decision changed, or new rule suggested. No-covariate models are primary; covariate models are secondary. Each model uses its own noncore population. The pre-RMSE percentile reference and all flags are **frozen at their original full-half values**: deletion removes counties from both arms and does not re-screen remaining counties.

For each simulation, aggregate error is the mean retained signed county error. Each county's exact squared-error contribution is aggregate error × county error / retained count. County contributions are averaged across the same usable simulations, assigning zero when a county is absent or excluded. Their sum equals MSE. Shares are **signed**: cancellation can produce negative contributions, and top positive shares can exceed 100%. Empty retained samples yield unavailable errors, not zero error; usable and paired simulation counts are exported.

## Concentration of unscreened MSE

Top shares here rank counties by their MSE contributions. “Counties to 50” is the first cumulative share reaching 50%. The full CSV includes top-5/top-10 shares and all four rules.

## Top-five influential county profiles

These counties rank by the **decrease in unscreened RMSE when removed**, with county ID breaking ties. Negative decreases identify protective/cancelling counties. This ranking differs from contribution ranking because deletion also changes the county denominator. Expected pre-period count and size stratum are the unchanged saved assignment's main-TWFE-MAR reference. Outcome-age population is saved exposure `n`, averaged over all finite panel years for that county. Pseudo-treated frequency uses all pseudo-treated rows; error and flag summaries condition on an eligible available-window target. Unconditional all-simulation flag rates are also exported. A county is marked recurrent when it appears among the top five in at least two models within the same half/scenario/branch.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## A/B ratios before and after deleting top counties

Each half/model/scenario uses its own unscreened-influence ranking to delete the top one or three counties from **both** unscreened and screened arms wherever they appear. The original masks remain fixed. The complete leave-one-out CSV ranks both signed unscreened-RMSE decreases and the magnitude of ratio changes. Shrinkage is a descriptive reduction in the absolute difference between A and B ratios, not a significance test. Tables include all six models; the summary of operational-screen differences averages the five non-TWFE models equally across scenarios.

::: {.panel-tabset}


:::

## Interpretation

Positive-contribution capture weights eligible top-five county appearances by the positive part of their **unscreened** aggregate-error contribution. It measures whether flags coincide with influential error realizations; it is not a causal decomposition of the screening gain. The rates below average model/scenario cells equally.

```{r interpretation, results='asis'}
cat(paste0('- ',influence_summary_lines(x),collapse='\n'),'\n')
```

## Checks and downloads

The exact county contributions sum to MSE within numerical precision. Full-population signed errors, retained counts, RMSEs, RMSE ratios and their MC SEs reproduce the stored A/B estimates for all rules and both branches. A-only/B-only assignment and hash guards run at entry and exit. Raw main-fit contents are never opened: cached cumulative totals are reused, and fit metadata is checked only for cache provenance. Every original output and the decision are protected by checksums.

```{r numerical-check-summary}
knitr::kable(x$checks[,.(comparisons=.N,max_abs_difference=max(max_abs_difference),within_precision=all(within_precision)),by=quantity],digits=15)
```
